title: DDGAD: Disagreement-Driven Graph Anomaly Detection via Adapt-Then-Combine
abstract: arXiv:2605.26446v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Graph anomaly detection (GAD) commonly relies on message passing to jointly encode node attributes and neighborhood context. However, once the two are mixed, an abnormal post-encoding state may reflect either an intrinsic node deviation or incompatible contextual influence, making its source ambiguous. We propose Disagreement-Driven Graph Anomaly Detection (DDGAD), which treats persistent incompatibility between node-wise and contextual estimates as anomaly evidence. Inspired by Adapt-Then-Combine (ATC), DDGAD reverses its consensus objective: Adapt produces a node-wise estimate without new same-step neighbor aggregation, while Combine forms a neighborhood-dependent contextual estimate, and their pre-consensus disagreement is accumulated across ATC steps for detection. We further characterize this signal from graph-spectral and source-response perspectives and derive sufficient conditions for anomaly--normal separation under contextu

translated_title: DDGAD：基于“适应-组合”框架的分歧驱动图异常检测
translated_abstract: 图异常检测（GAD）通常依赖消息传递来联合编码节点属性与邻域上下文。然而，一旦两者混合，编码后的异常状态可能既反映节点自身的内在偏离，也可能反映不相容的上下文影响，使其异常来源变得模糊不清。我们提出分歧驱动图异常检测方法DDGAD，该方法将节点级估计与上下文估计之间持续存在的不相容性作为异常证据。受“适应-组合”（Adapt-Then-Combine, ATC）框架启发，DDGAD颠倒了其原有的共识目标：Adapt（适应）阶段在不进行同步骤邻居聚合的情况下产生节点级估计，而Combine（组合）阶段则形成依赖于邻域的上下文估计，两者在达成共识之前的分歧会在多个ATC步骤中不断累积，并用于异常检测。我们进一步从图谱和源响应的视角对该信号进行表征，并在上下文条件下推导出异常节点与正常节点可分离的充分条件。
tldr: 提出DDGAD方法，通过“适应-组合”框架分别生成节点级估计与上下文估计，并将两者间持续累积的分歧作为异常证据，从而解决了传统消息传递中节点异常与上下文异常来源混淆的问题。
en_tdlr: DDGAD detects graph anomalies by separately producing node-wise and contextual estimates through an Adapt-Then-Combine framework, treating their persistently accumulated disagreement as anomaly evidence to resolve the source ambiguity caused by entangled message passing.
